[The reset]{.kicker}

## This is not a software course

This course is not organized around software demos.

It is organized around one question:

::: {.concept-card}
[The course question]{.card-title}
**What evidence would make a design decision more defensible?**
:::

Every tool we touch is judged only by how well it answers that.

## One method, four objects

The same four-step move repeats all semester. Only the **object** changes — and each phase's weekly work accumulates into one assignment.

| Phase | Weeks | You reconstruct… | Builds |
|---|---|---|---|
| A1 | 1–3 | a **past decision** + its evidence | Total Recall board |
| A2 | 4–6 | candidate **tools / routes** | Evidence + Workflow Map |
| A3 | 7–9 | your **prototype** running | Prototype + Verification |
| A4 | 10–12 | the **package** you hand over | Workflow Package |

[The recurring engine]{.kicker}

## Look harder at what you already did

You learn most by examining the reasoning inside work you have **already done** — not by adding new work. Every week, the same four questions, pointed at that week's object:

::: {.recall-4step}
::: {.step}
**Did** What did I actually do, step by step?
:::
::: {.step}
**Assumed** What did I assume at each step?
:::
::: {.step}
**Risk** Where did I not check — where could it break?
:::
::: {.step}
**Verify** What would I verify if I did it again?
:::
:::

The point is not to judge old work. It is to see how its argument was built.

---

## Evidence needs a workflow

- precedent images can be useful, but rarely prove performance on their own
- simulation numbers can be precise, but still depend on assumptions
- survey comments can be rich, but need context before they generalize
- data only becomes useful when the path from input to decision is legible

::: {.concept-card}
A finding is evidence only when someone else can inspect how you got it.
:::

---

## Sometimes evidence is just vibes

:::: {.two-col}
::: {.example-card}
[A vibe is not useless]{.card-title}
It is often the first clue that something might matter.
:::

::: {.warning-card}
[A vibe is not enough by itself]{.card-title}
It gets stronger only when the next step asks what would confirm, qualify, or challenge it.
:::
::::

For each image next: name the **vibe claim**, **what it does not show yet**, and the **next evidence move**.

---

## Vibe case 1: busy = working?

::: {.vibe-case}
::: {.vibe-visual}
![Polished restaurant interior, dramatic lighting, visually busy](../assets/generated/vibes-evidence/restaurant-vibe.png)
:::
::: {.vibe-panel}
[Let the class answer first]{.vibe-kicker}

::: {.fragment .example-card}
**Vibe claim:** "This layout works; it feels busy."
:::
::: {.fragment .warning-card}
**Not shown yet:** atmosphere is not a measured use pattern.
:::
::: {.fragment .activity-card}
**Ask for:** dwell time, table turnover, circulation pinch points, observation by time period.
:::
:::
:::

---

## Vibe case 2: polished = high performance?

::: {.vibe-case}
::: {.vibe-visual}
![Smartphone camera preview of a picturesque mountain and lake](../assets/generated/vibes-evidence/phone-camera-vibe.png)
:::
::: {.vibe-panel}
[The ad-logic problem]{.vibe-kicker}

::: {.fragment .example-card}
**Vibe claim:** "This camera is good; the image looks amazing."
:::
::: {.fragment .warning-card}
**Not shown yet:** presentation polish is not performance.
:::
::: {.fragment .activity-card}
**Ask for:** controlled comparisons, low-light tests, compression checks, failure cases.
:::
:::
:::

---

## Vibe case 3: calm = safer?

::: {.vibe-case}
::: {.vibe-visual}
![French street at blue hour with trees, lamps, calm road](../assets/generated/vibes-evidence/calm-route-vibe.png)
:::
::: {.vibe-panel}
[Perception is partial]{.vibe-kicker}

::: {.fragment .example-card}
**Vibe claim:** "This route is safer; it feels calmer."
:::
::: {.fragment .warning-card}
**Not shown yet:** perceived calm may miss actual risk.
:::
::: {.fragment .activity-card}
**Ask for:** lighting levels, pedestrian counts, crossing conflicts, incident records.
:::
:::
:::

---

## Vibe case 4: green = sustainable?

::: {.vibe-case}
::: {.vibe-visual}
![Greenery-covered building facade with dense planted wall](../assets/generated/vibes-evidence/green-facade-vibe.png)
:::
::: {.vibe-panel}
[The studio render problem]{.vibe-kicker}

::: {.fragment .example-card}
**Vibe claim:** "This facade is sustainable; the render is green."
:::
::: {.fragment .warning-card}
**Not shown yet:** visual greenness is not environmental performance.
:::
::: {.fragment .activity-card}
**Ask for:** solar exposure, heat gain, daylight, irrigation/maintenance, material data.
:::
:::
:::

---

## Workflow routes, not software shopping

- **GH / parametric** — vary design options
- **BIM/BEM / simulation** — test performance assumptions
- **GIS** — compare spatial conditions
- **Python / notebook** — rerun analysis and figures
- **AI-assisted** — speed up components, then verify
- **Spreadsheet / low-code** — compare ranges and thresholds transparently

::: {.reflection-card}
Not "which software looks advanced?" but "which workflow makes this decision more defensible?"
:::

---

[The GH bridge]{.kicker}

## Every pathway can talk to Grasshopper

Most of you will return to Grasshopper. That is fine. The point is to make the route into a clean function before it becomes a component.

::: {.bridge-flow}
::: {.node .current}
external workflow
:::
::: {.node}
visible output change
:::
::: {.node}
CSV / JSON / GeoJSON
:::
::: {.node}
GH read / GhPython
:::
::: {.node}
design action
:::
:::

::: {.function-contract}
**Grasshopper component = packed function**
Inputs go in, an operation happens inside, outputs come out. The course asks you to name the inputs, units, ranges, output, and quality check before you trust the component.
:::

[The uncertainty habit]{.kicker}

## The course contribution

Tools make outputs look certain. Architecture usually is not.

::: {.uncertainty-check}
**Ask every week**
What did the tool make easier to see, and what assumption did it make easier to hide?
:::

I am at the table too: I declare, I walk through, and I get audited like everyone else.

## Round table on YOUR evidence

::: {.spine-rail}
[Decision]{.node} [Evidence]{.node .is-current} [Variation]{.node} [Output]{.node} [Threshold]{.node} [Action]{.node}
:::

Upload one rough visual (render, sketch, diagram, table, screenshot), then we work in two modes. [feeds A1]{.feeds-tag}

---

## Mode 1 — the walk-through (optional, celebrated)

::: {.walkthrough-card}
[Teach us your strongest tool]{.card-title}
A volunteer shows the class one tool they know well — uninterrupted, 3–4 minutes. This is teaching, and we treat it as such.
:::

- not graded as a performance; volunteering earns credit, never penalty
- the room listens; questions wait for Mode 2
- no polish required — show the real thing working

---

## Mode 2 — the audit (everyone)

::: {.audit-card}
[Examine the work, not the person]{.card-title}
We ask the same question of every artifact, including mine: **what does this actually show, and what does it not show yet?**
:::

- the strongest move is naming your own weakest link first
- we challenge the **claim**, never your competence
- volunteers go first; a random draw fills the remaining examples

---

## Reconstruct your decision in four steps

**Object this week: one past studio decision and its evidence.**

::: {.recall-4step}
::: {.step}
**Did** What did I decide, and what did I actually do?
:::
::: {.step}
**Assumed** What did I treat as evidence that was really assumption or precedent?
:::
::: {.step}
**Risk** Where was confidence stronger than the evidence?
:::
::: {.step}
**Verify** What evidence would I gather for the next decision?
:::
:::

::: {.grading-note}
Post your filled four-step to Slack under your image. Posting + an honest reconstruction is the graded unit — not how you spoke.
:::

[Where we are headed]{.kicker}

## What success looks like

By Week 12 you should be able to say, about one real decision:

::: {.concept-card}
**This is the decision, this is the evidence, this is the method, and this is how confident I am.**
:::

Use the [Total Recall Board](../templates/total-recall-board.md) to start A1.
